# AI-Powered Legal Tech Startup Lucio Raises $5 Mn

 07 Oct'25 | By Bhupendra Paintola 

 

Bengaluru-based legal tech AI startup Lucio has secured $5 Mn in its seed round led by DeVC, with participation from Lucky Investment Managers’ cofounder Ashish Kacholia and Alchemy Capital Management’s cofounder Lashit Sanghvi.

The startup plans to use the fresh funds to expand its product lineup, deepen AI-powered personalisation for legal workflows, and accelerate its global adoption.

Founded by lawyers Vasu Aggarwal and Darsan Guruvayurappan in 2022, Lucio offers an AI-native workspace tailored for the legal sector. The platform claims to support more than 200 organisations and over 3,000 lawyers across nine jurisdictions. 

It helps lawyers with document review, drafting, due diligence, legal research, and translation, and claims to help save an average of 30 hours per lawyer every month.

The funding comes at a time when AI adoption is rising rapidly across sectors. As a result, a number of legal tech startups have also emerged which are helping automate processes like contract drafting, legal briefs, opinions and filings. These legal tech startups are also attracting strong investor interest.

For instance, SpotDraft raised $54 Mn from Temasek subsidiary Vertex Growth and Trident Partners in February. In 2024, Info Edge announced plans to invest INR 4 Cr in its portfolio company LegitQuest, while AI-powered startup Jhana.ai secured $1.6 Mn in its maiden round led by Together Fund.

At the heart of this trend lies India’s rapidly expanding GenAI ecosystem, projected to become a $17 Bn opportunity by 2030. Moreover, investor confidence in the sector is evident from the over $1.6 Bn raised by AI-native startups between 2022 and Q3 2025. 

In a recent survey conducted by Inc42, 41% of investors said they have allocated up to 40% of their portfolio to AI-focussed companies. However, only 7% consider AI a core investment focus.

Bar & Bench

Published on: 

08 Oct 2025, 1:24 pm

Lucio, a leading AI-native legal workspace built by lawyers, has raised $5 million from a fundraise led by DeVC and HNIs Ashish Kacholia and Lashit Sanghvi.

The $5 million round will enable Lucio to achieve two critical objectives: first, expanding Lucio’s product offerings to embed legal AI into every interface where lawyers work; and second, deepening its personalization capabilities to provide lawyers across jurisdictions with a highly tailored, friction-free AI experience.

Vasu Aggarwal, co-founder of Lucio, shared,

“Most legal tech doesn't fail in demos, it fails at desks. We are building Lucio to disappear into legal workflows, to meet lawyers where they already are, elevate the quality of their output, and make them fall in love with the law again.”

Darsan Guruvayurappan, co-founder of Lucio, added,

“Legal AI isn’t just about efficiency, it’s about reimagining the experience for clients, attorneys, and all other stakeholders in the practice of law. Our investor' trust and investment give us the ability to take our mission across the world.”

Adopted by 200+ organisations worldwide, including enterprise law firms, in-house teams, and boutique firms, Lucio supports over 3000 lawyers across 9 jurisdictions.

Lawyers use Lucio for drafting, reviewing large document sets, due diligence, legal research, and translation, saving an average of 30 hours per lawyer each month.

# Lucio Raises $5M in Funding

-

October 8, 2025

Lucio, a Bengaluru, India-based provider of an AI-native legal workspace built by lawyers, raised $5M in funding.

The round was led by DeVC and HNIs Ashish Kacholia and Lashit Sanghvi.

The company intends to use the funds to achieve two critical objectives:

- first, expand it product offerings to embed legal AI into every interface where lawyers work;
- and second to enhance its personalization capabilities to provide lawyers across jurisdictions with a friction-free AI experience.

Co-founded by Vasu Aggarwal, and Darsan Guruvayurappan, Lucio provides an AI-native legal workspace with an adoption-first design that allows personalization and advanced legal reasoning. Lawyers use it for drafting, reviewing large document sets, due diligence, legal research, and translation, saving an average of 30 hours per lawyer each month.

Adopted by 200+ organisations worldwide, including enterprise law firms, in-house teams, and boutique firms, Lucio supports over 3000 lawyers across 9 jurisdictions.

highlights:
Lucio Raises $5 Million in Funding

Lucio, a Bengaluru, India-based AI-native legal workspace built by lawyers, has raised $5 million in funding.

## Investors

The round was led by DeVC and high-net-worth individuals Ashish Kacholia and Lashit Sanghvi.

Decentralized Venture Capital (DeVC) is a Bengaluru, India-based pre-seed venture capital firm founded in 2022. The firm invests in very early-stage startups (pre-seed/seed) across sectors, including SaaS, fintech, and climate tech.

Ashish Kacholia is the founder of Lucky Investment Managers and a proprietary investor in the Indian equity markets.

Lashit Sanghvi is an entrepreneur and angel investor. He is the co-founder and Non-Executive Director of Alchemy Capital Management Private Limited.

## Lucio Use of Funds

The company will use the new capital to expand its product offerings, embed AI more deeply into legal workflows, and enhance personalization for lawyers across global jurisdictions.

## About Lucio

Lucio AI is an AI-powered workspace specifically designed to accelerate legal intelligence for lawyers, law firms, and in-house legal teams. It helps lawyers draft documents, review large datasets, conduct due diligence, perform legal research, and translate materials efficiently. Adopted by more than 200 organizations worldwide and supports over 3,000 lawyers across nine jurisdictions. Lucio’s mission is to continue innovating to meet the practice-specific needs of lawyers and to expand that vision globally.
